newsitem.title: USA: Apple CFO sees 20 pct+ gross margins.
newsitem.headline: Apple CFO sees 20 pct+ gross margins.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Chief Financial Officer Fred Anderson said on Tuesday he expects the company to maintain gross profit margins of 20 percent or better.
Appearing on CNBC's "Squawk Box" television program, Anderson said, "We believe that we can sustain gross margins above 20 percent going forward."

He was responding to a question about whether the company expected to increase its gross margins above the roughly 22 percent margins it reported in results for its fiscal fourth quarter ended in September.
In the latest quarter, the company startled Wall Street by reporting a profit of $0.06 per share, after restructuring expenses, compared to analysts' consensus estimate of a loss of $0.30 per share.

Anderson left open the possiblity that future versions of Apple's Macintosh operating system could be based on a highly regarded new operating system from Be Inc, a start-up software maker founded by a former Apple executive.
He declined to comment directly on reports that Apple is interested in buying Be's innovative software technology.

Speaking of Apple's plans for its Macintosh operating system, Anderson said, "We're committed to bringing a modern Mac OS out in six-month increments -- new releases -- over the next year and a half or so."

"Part of it's a make-buy decision," he said, referring to Apple's choice of whether to develop refinements to its Macintosh operating system in-house or to buy elements of, or an entirely new operating system, from outside the company.

"We look at technology components that we need for the new (Operating System) and we have a lot of creative engineers that can develop it, but it becomes a time-to-market issue," he told CNBC interviewers.
"So you have to evaluate everything that's out there, and I wouldn't specifically comment on Be or any other software developer out there," Anderson said.
Apple has struggled in recent years to differentiate its Macintosh operating system from Microsoft Corp's graphically based Windows operating systems.
Be, founded by former Apple executive Jean-Louis Gassee when he left Apple in 1990, makes a line of powerful desktop computers geared for use by software developers and multimedia artists.
